eligibility: The three-volume A Mathematical Gift is a set of Kyoto lectures prepared for classroom use by mathematics teachers and undergraduates. Worked development of surfaces, dimension, elliptic functions and algebraic geometry is reinforced by exercises. Its friendly style does not change its course-study structure.
reason: Hard-exclude the nominated three-volume instructional work. The AMS descriptions explicitly identify the classroom audience and exercises, including the staged derivation of the Poncelet theorem in volume II.

eligibility: The Grothendieck–Serre Correspondence reproduces mathematical research letters, with later technical notes. Its main content is specialist discussion of schemes, sheaves, cohomology and algebraic geometry, rather than an explanatory biography for readers outside specialist work.
reason: Hard-exclude the research correspondence in its nominated scope. The historical and personal context is valuable but subsidiary to the technical exchanges. The science-biography exception to V3 does not override H2.

eligibility: Schroeder's Number Theory in Science and Communication develops number-theoretic tools and their use in computation, cryptography and signal design. The publisher identifies it as a textbook; its thirty-chapter structure progresses through fundamentals, congruences, residue methods, transforms and application techniques.
reason: Hard-exclude on the combined evidence of its instructional and technical-reference structure. The intended non-mathematician audience consists largely of scientific users of the methods; intuitive exposition, anecdotes and broad applications do not remove the specialist-method purpose.

eligibility: Moriyasu's primer is designed to give readers with quantum-mechanics training an introductory working account of gauge theory. After a historical opening, it develops local transformations, connections, gauge fields, symmetry breaking, electroweak unification, color and topology in a sequential technical exposition.
reason: Hard-exclude this specialist introductory primer. Its physical intuition and historical material help teach the field; they do not turn its main structure into a general-reader history. Confidence is moderate because the author also stresses appreciation for nonexperts.
